clue.text: "What _____" and "What _____ next" — a 21 16 across

definitions.meaning: the gaps complete the titles of Susan Coolidge's children's novels about Katy Carr, read as two words
the cross-references make a grasshopper (21 GRAS + 16 SHOPPER), and this American insect is a long-horned grasshopper

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blanks quiz on two old children's book titles, answered by naming an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What Katy Did' and 'What Katy Did Next' are classic American girls' novels; the insect is named for its call, which sounds like 'Katy did'.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American insect is a kind of long-horned grasshopper, so it is an example of the cross-referenced creature.

clue.text: The excitement of the beautiful game

definitions.meaning: getting your thrills is getting your ...
football, 'the beautiful game', is played with blows of the foot on the ball

explanation.surface: Someone describing the thrill of watching football.
explanation.definitionFit: Kicks is informal for thrills, and kicks are also the strikes of the ball that make up a football match.

clue.text: Broken toe (including nail) on which arrows descended

indicators.note: the rearranged toe wraps around the nail, holding it inside
a broken toe is a damaged one, so its letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: a stud is a nail with a large head

explanation.surface: A medical note about a broken toe, nail and all, bizarrely followed by a hail of arrows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' scrambles the toe and 'including' wraps it round the nail. The testudo was the Roman 'tortoise' formation, soldiers' shields locked overhead against arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman testudo was a roof of overlapping shields that soldiers held over their heads to ward off arrows and missiles.

clue.text: Man's follower, best between 10 and 10

definitions.meaning: the letters that come after Man in the name of Nelson Mandela
the French phrase for the very best is crème ___ crème, and 10 is CREME, so these words sit between two of it

explanation.surface: A puzzling note about who comes after a man and what lies between two tens.
explanation.walkthrough: The light is French for 'of the'; 'Man's follower' is the rest of MANDELA, and 'crème de la crème' means the pick of the bunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase completes Mandela after Man, and completes the French idiom for the elite between two creams.

clue.text: Cornish Eve, flighty in fancy, takes neighbour's product

indicators.note: the Cornish Eve is put inside the dream before the whole lot is scrambled

parts.note: a fancy is a daydream or reverie, a dream

indicators.note: a flighty mind is fickle and scattered, so the letters fly into a new order

explanation.surface: A capricious Cornishwoman dreamily enjoys a delicacy from the county next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty' scrambles the Cornish Eve once placed 'in' the dream. Devon is Cornwall's neighbour in south-west England, and the two counties argue over who makes the better clotted cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Devon borders Cornwall in south-west England, and its thick clotted cream is the famous produce of the neighbouring county.

clue.text: See 10
9, 10 5 across, and 24 21's language needing refinement? You can do it on the table

definitions.text: You can do it on the table

parts.note: the three cross-referenced phrases are all French, so their language is French
refining something is polishing it up

explanation.surface: Three French phrases are said to need tidying, with a hint about furniture care.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrases at 9, 10/5 and 24/21 are French; that language 'needing refinement' wants polishing. French polishing is a shellac finish applied to wooden furniture such as tables.
explanation.definitionFit: French polishing gives wooden furniture a high-gloss shellac finish, so it is something done to a dining table.

clue.text: Charge copyright to America in case

indicators.note: copyright and America are put inside the case

parts.note: a legal case is an action at law
C is the symbol for copyright, ©
USA, the United States of America

explanation.surface: A lawyer levels a charge of copyright breach against America in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a charge against someone is to make an accusation of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Make round number burn

indicators.note: make goes round the number, enclosing it

parts.note: to make is to create
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: An instruction to round off a number and set fire to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like it describes the number, but it puts CREATE around M.
explanation.definitionFit: To cremate is to burn a corpse to ashes.

clue.text: It was there (it was said) the day before the sabbath?

parts.note: the eve is the day before a festival
the sabbath is the day of rest

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that existed on the day before the holy day.
explanation.walkthrough: George Mallory, asked why he wanted to climb this mountain, reportedly said 'Because it's there'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallory's famous quip about climbing the world's highest mountain was that it was there.

clue.text: A vile sect makes a verbal 22

indicators.note: the words a vile sect are made into something else, a reworking of their letters

explanation.surface: A wicked cult produces a spoken gesture of indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is SHRUG: the French 'that's life' is a shrug put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase meaning 'such is life' is a resigned spoken equivalent of shrugging the shoulders.

clue.text: 11 end of 4 gives me fair play in the nursery

indicators.note: the rearranged words go inside the nursery

parts.note: a crèche is a nursery for young children

indicators.note: letters at play move about freely, so me fair is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is promised fair treatment when playing in a nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' scrambles 'me fair', and 'in' puts the result inside the nursery word. 11 is SOUR and the end of 4 is CREAM: the French dairy product is soured cream.
explanation.definitionFit: This thick French dairy product is cream soured with a bacterial culture, so it is a sour cream.

clue.text: Point on which the Guardian's embittered

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
the newspaper speaking of itself says our

explanation.surface: A remark about the matter on which the Guardian newspaper feels resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle is printed in the Guardian, so the paper's own possessive is OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sour person is bitter and resentful, as embittered people are.

clue.text: How much in an Eastern Catholic is having one rib?

indicators.note: the price is put inside the Eastern Catholic

parts.note: a Uniate belongs to an Eastern church in communion with Rome
asking how much is asking the cost

explanation.surface: A question about the price of something owned by an Eastern church member, oddly with a single rib.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a leaf with a single midrib is described with this term, from Latin uni- one and costa rib.

clue.text: Dreadful slump in voice production that can't be helped?

indicators.note: something dreadful is a mess, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A singer's terrible decline in vocal production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' is a link to the definition; put SLUMP into VOICE and 'Dreadful' rearranges all ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Compulsive behaviour is driven by an irresistible urge, so the person cannot help doing it.

clue.text: Doctor the water to find a lizard

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is an army doctor
a loch is a Scottish lake, a stretch of water

explanation.surface: A medic treats the lake water and finds a reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a verb meaning tamper with, but it gives MO.
explanation.definitionFit: The moloch, or thorny devil, is a spiny Australian lizard.

clue.text: Bond in a singular garment is a sick man

indicators.note: the bond goes inside the garment

parts.note: pants are a plural garment, so a single one is a pant
a tie is a bond that binds

explanation.surface: James Bond, oddly dressed in a single item of clothing, turns out to be ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests the spy, but it is TIE, a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient is someone ill who is receiving medical treatment.

clue.text: Actor Anthony is without work; page the customer

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the actor surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Sir Antony Sher was a celebrated British stage actor
OP, opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: An out-of-work actor pages a customer in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but has its old sense of outside: the actor wraps the work and the page.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopper is a customer going round the shops to buy things.

clue.text: Typically happy adult who puts children to sleep

definitions.meaning: the proverbially happy one is a sandboy, so the grown-up version is the man
the folklore figure who sprinkles sand in children's eyes to make them drowsy

explanation.surface: A cheerful grown-up whose job is putting children to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy as a sandboy' is a British saying for being carefree.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore this figure sprinkles sleepy dust in children's eyes at bedtime.

clue.text: Elements of cricket go too far

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
a run is a unit of scoring in cricket

explanation.surface: Parts of a cricket match go on too long.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is six deliveries from one end; a run is scored by batters running between the wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to go beyond a set limit or time.

clue.text: A scrubber (John take note)

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, a loo
fah is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A bracketed reminder to John about a cleaning implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' reads as a name but is slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is a dried gourd sponge used to scrub the skin in the bath.

clue.text: Coming of one of three, it is said (or rather sung)

indicators.note: the words are spoken, or sung, so the sound of a phrase gives the entry

parts.note: in an eternal triangle of three people, one is a rival

explanation.surface: The appearance of one of a trio is announced, or rather chanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A rival', one member of a love triangle, sounds like the entry; the '(or rather sung)' playfully excuses a slurred match.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is a coming, the act of reaching a place.

clue.text: Want right to hold property about a century, which includes the sewers

parts.note: to want is to need

indicators.note: the lease goes about the century, enclosing it

parts.note: a lease grants the right to hold property for a term

explanation.surface: A tenant wants a property lease running about a hundred years, sewers included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewers' reads as drains but means people who sew: their needles live in this holder.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle-case holds sewing needles, the tools of those who sew.

clue.text: See 24
Don't talk to the carpet, it shows you don't care

parts.note: sh is a call for silence
a rug is a small carpet

explanation.surface: Someone told off for talking to the carpet replies with indifference.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising the shoulders in a shrug is a gesture of indifference.

clue.text: The fool in 4

definitions.meaning: British slang for a stupid person
4 is Devonshire, or clotted, cream, and a ... is one of the thickened lumps found in it

explanation.surface: A dessert called fool is found in Devon's famous cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fool' teases as the creamy British pudding of that name, but it means an idiot; the second sense is a thick lump forming in scalded cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Clot is British slang for a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Feast like artists in a heavenly body

indicators.note: the liking and the artists go inside the planet

parts.note: Mars is a planet, a heavenly body
dig is slang for like
RA, Royal Academicians, are artists

explanation.surface: A celebration where people enjoy artists on a planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' reads as 'similar to' but is the verb, slang DIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras, Shrove Tuesday, is a carnival feast day before Lent begins.

clue.text: He's bad either way, right?

parts.note: evil means bad

indicators.note: the same word read in both directions, so it is given forwards then backwards

parts.note: evil means bad

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about someone who is wicked whichever way you look.
explanation.walkthrough: EVIL forwards and backwards gives EVIL LIVE, then R for 'right' completes it: the whole clue describes the wrongdoer.
explanation.definitionFit: An evil-liver is someone who leads a wicked life.

clue.text: Old-time vacation, standard form of 10 included

indicators.note: the reshaped number is included in the standard

parts.note: a norm is a standard

indicators.note: a new form of the number means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the figure read as the number ten, not a cross-reference

explanation.surface: Holidays of old, with a standard version of the tenth item included.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a reference to the CREME light, but it is just the number, which 'form of' rearranges before it is 'included' in the standard.
explanation.definitionFit: In old university usage a non-term was the vacation period outside term time.

clue.text: Joke about the box on the table?

indicators.note: the joke goes about the television, wrapping it

parts.note: a gag is a joke
the box is slang for the television, the telly or tele

explanation.surface: A gag about the TV set sitting on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: A gateleg table has hinged legs that swing out like a gate to support the folding leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateleg is the swinging leg that props up the drop leaf of a table.
